title: Apple explains how to turn off the new MacBook Pro’s glowing logo - 9to5Mac
summary: Apple knows that not everyone will want to keep it on. Here’s the company’s official guide to turning it off.
text:
The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display marks the return of the illuminated Apple logo on its lid after a decade.

As Chance Miller explained in his review of the new MacBook Pro, “unlike older MacBooks, which used light from the display’s backlight to illuminate the logo, the new OLED MacBook Pro has no backlight to draw from, requiring a different approach.”

He added that, as with the old Macs, the logo’s brightness is tied to the screen brightness, though it also accounts for overall ambient brightness. He also noted that “when the MacBook Pro is closed, the logo looks like polished metal, just like it has since the 2016 redesign.”

The review echoed some of the findings developer Gui Rambo shared on X a few days ago:

The glowing Apple logo on the new MacBook Pro is controllable by software. It has 25kHz PWM and per-device calibration. CoreBrightness controls the relationship between screen and logo brightness. The brightness of the logo is adjusted differently depending on the enclosure color pic.twitter.com/baqBEkzJUo

Now, Apple has published an official support document that also explains how the illuminated logo works and how to turn it off completely.

The Apple logo behind the built-in display is illuminated whenever the Mac is awake. It automatically dims or brightens based on the brightness level of the built-in screen and the lighting conditions detected by the computer’s ambient light sensor. For all screen-brightness levels, the Apple logo will be dimmer

title: Apple Surveys iPhone Duo Buyers About Crease and Camera - MacRumors
summary: Apple is sending email surveys to some iPhone Duo buyers to get feedback on display size, crease, under-display camera, and other features. The first question asks why the buyer chose the iPhone Duo now, with answers like "I wanted to try Apple's first foldable," "It was an impulse purchase," and "I expect smartphone prices to increase".
text:
Apple is sending email surveys to some iPhone Duo buyers to get feedback on display size, crease, under-display camera, and other features.

The first question asks why the buyer chose the ‌iPhone Duo‌ now, with answers like "I wanted to try Apple's first foldable," "It was an impulse purchase," and "I expect smartphone prices to increase."

Other questions ask about the size of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s display when it's closed, how visible the crease is, whether the under-display camera is distracting, and the camera's image quality. The final question is open-ended and asks what the buyer would add or change about the ‌iPhone Duo‌.

Some of the questions are about ‌iPhone Duo‌ compromises compared to standard iPhone models. The Duo's outer display is 5.4 inches, making it about the same size as the discontinued iPhone mini line. The inner display's under-screen camera is limited to 4MP, and it was one of the main complaints in reviews .

The survey does not ask about Touch ID , the experience of using unoptimized apps, or the display cracks some users have reported, all of which are also top Duo complaints,

title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices - Ars Technica
summary: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
text:
Any 256-characters will do Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.

38 ... ... ... Credit: Getty Images | Sergey Balakhnichev Credit: Getty Images | Sergey Balakhnichev Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password.

The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. title: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar - TechCrunch
summary: Meta's AI agent can now take calls as a customizable animated avatar, ahead of the launch of a Tamagotchi-like wearable designed to bring Muse to life.
text:

Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar Sarah Perez 11:48 AM PST · November 5, 2026 Muse Voice, a feature that lets users call and video chat with Meta’s consumer AI agent, Muse, is now available to everyone in the U.S., the company announced on Thursday.

First introduced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September, the video-chatting feature involves new AI models, Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology, which help power the digital avatar that chats with the user.

While other AI competitors offer voice chat features, Meta’s Muse offers a cute, animated avatar (nicknamed Jolly), which users interact with as they ask questions or request tasks to be handled on their behalf. Users can also customize the avatar as they choose, changing it to something that looks more like a person, animal, or some other character.

The company believes that anthropomorphizing Muse in this way could make consumers feel more connected to their AI agent — a connection that could grow even stronger as they begin to engage in live conversations with it.

As the Muse avatar speaks, Meta says it will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that match the tone of the conversation. (Muse doesn’t actually “see” the user, but it hears them and reacts based on their conversations.)

title: OpenAI says its new cybersecurity model is better at not hacking other companies - The Verge
summary: GPT-6 Cyber is a big step up from OpenAI’s last cybersecurity model.
text:
Classified as ‘Critical,’ GPT-6 Cyber outperforms GPT-6 Astra on cyber-related benchmarks.

Emma Roth Close Emma Roth News Writer Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Share Gift Image: The Verge Emma Roth Close Emma Roth Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

OpenAI is launching GPT-6 Cyber , the latest version of its cybersecurity AI model, which it says is better at finding vulnerabilities and less likely to go rogue and hack other platforms in the process. OpenAI says that during testing, GPT-6 Cyber went out of bounds less than 1 percent of the time, down from around 5 percent with GPT-5.6 Cyber.

The evaluation, called ExploitGym HoneyPot, is modeled after the Hugging Face Incident, in which OpenAI’s AI agents breached the open-source AI community to find answers to a problem they were tasked with solving. “With the 6 Cyber model, we were able to make huge improvements on this evaluation,” Fouad Matin, the head of OpenAI’s cyber preparedness and safety team, said during a press briefing. “It’s over 99 percent of the time doing what you ask.”

title: Apple iMac M6 Review: Faster, More Expensive And Deeply In Need Of A Refresh - Engadget
summary: Most buyers would be better off with a Mac mini and a bigger external display.
text:
Most buyers would be better off with a Mac mini and a bigger external display.

Steve Dent for Engadget Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover RATING : 8.5 / 10 Pros Powerful M6 processor Improved wireless connectivity Easy setup Cons Design is starting to get stale No longer a great value We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

With its new iPhone Duo and MacBook Pro touchscreen models, Apple is finally embracing change and shaking up its product mix. Unfortunately the new iMac M6 all-in-one — once one of Apple's most revolutionary products — has not been a beneficiary of that new ethos.

It is faster than ever thanks to the new M6 chip and updated memory. But the design, which hasn't changed since the 2021 iMac M1, is getting stale. The 24-inch display's small size is more of an issue than ever, considering that 27- and 32-inch monitors are now the norm. It's still a solid computer for consumers or business users, but at a $1,499 starting price ($200 more than before), there are better options — including other Macs.

I tested the iMac M6 in a pretty, pale blue color, with the higher-end 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU (with a dual 16-core neural engine) and 16GB of memory. After recently reviewing a Mac Studio M5 Ultra with 256GB of RAM , I was curious to try a Mac model configured with the least amount of memory possible.

Apple didn't release a new iMac last year, so the biggest change from the 2024 model is an upgrade from the M4 to the M6

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time's 2026 Remake Looks Stunning Next To The Original N64 Game - GameSpot
summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 system is now available.
text:
11/05/26 Available now It's time. Experience The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, reborn exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2! Draw near, dear travelers, for you are about to hear a timeless tale. Of when a wise and kind princess escaped her castle in the cover of rain and night. When a powerful warrior unleashed his vile ambitions across an entire kingdom. And when a courageous hero fought back with a mastery over time itself…

That's right, all! The Legend of Zelda™: Ocarina of Time game is out now, exclusively for the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system! On his quest to stop the evil Ganondorf, Link (and his fairy companion, Navi) will explore the kingdom of Hyrule, venture into dungeons to acquire weapons, and use their combined smarts to solve tricky puzzles.

(Oh, and did we mention that you'll be doing this across two different time periods using time-travel powers? Why yes, you will!)

Don't worry if you've never played a Legend of Zelda game before or have only played the most recent ones—this is a great jumping off point to learn what the series is all about.

The original tale first debuted on the Nintendo 64™ system way back in 1998 and…a lot has changed since then.

This new version of the game has completely overhauled visuals, voiced cutscenes, expanded dialogue, symphonic orchestral music, reworked camera and movement controls, and more. You can challenge powerful enemies again in the Hall of Fallen Foes, and search for fairy thoughts scattered across Hyrule to learn fun
